title: Compact whole-path baseline and summary residual
question: Does an independently trained summary encoder improve the same lightweight price model on R3's full OHLC return target?
configuration: RTX 4060; canonical screened C1; 35 observed and 140 future OHLC bars; seeds 0–2. The price + summary residual holds its same-seed price model fixed. All six checkpoints were selected by validation whole-path MAE and evaluated with a locked test configuration.
finding: Price + summary improved validation (82.403 vs. 82.626 bp) but not locked test (80.341 vs. 80.295 bp price-only, 80.487 zero; 2,236 events). Keep compact price-only as the forward baseline and evaluate further variants on validation.
limitations: Archive summaries, not original articles; forecast-time availability and near duplicates remain unverified. Test effects were mixed across seeds and no uncertainty interval was estimated. R3's published result is context only; per-event pairing and superiority over R3 were not independently established.

figure.alt: Across three validation seeds, adding event summaries lowered average full-path MAE from 82.626 to 82.403 basis points. The zero-return baseline was 83.636.

evidence.label: Locked test scores, provenance, and limits
